answer: Anchor three quartz-tipped buoys at the harbor's marked vertex, forming a triangle only real boats can reach. Each peer photographs its prism's dawn refraction from its assigned vertex, timestamped against the harbor tide table and a public webcam. Each buoy's $120 camera streams live, so a still must match the stream. Faking one vertex means chartering a boat ($400/day), forging a quartz prism ($180), and matching tide data within 2 minutes. Cloning 100 harbors costs $58,000 plus 90,000 POA locked 45 days and 30,000 burned per clone. A harbor admits only hulls that actually floated in.
